root_causes.evidence: 2016 online fraud: 85.9%, 2017 online fraud: 0.0%. 2016 chip fraud: 7.8%, 2017 chip fraud: 97.2%

root_causes.factor: No historical chip-fraud analogue in training
root_causes.evidence: Pre-2013 training has 0 chip fraud. 301 cases in 2014-2015 but adding them HURT 2017 transfer (Phase 14)

root_causes.factor: Feature out-of-support (2017 values outside pre-2016 range)
root_causes.evidence: Average 0.9% of 2017 chip fraud feature values outside pre-2016 support range

root_causes.factor: Pattern novelty (no pre-2016 analogue for most 2017 cases)
root_causes.evidence: 5.2% of 2017 chip fraud has no close pre-2016 neighbour

summary: The 2017 chip-fraud failure is primarily caused by a channel composition shift (online fraud disappeared, chip fraud appeared) combined with fundamental feature-distribution separation between training and 2017.
